summary: QMCtwin is a sign-problem-suppressed quantum Monte Carlo framework for master-equation simulation of QEC circuits that directly captures coherent, dissipative, and correlated noise dynamics beyond Pauli approximations. Applied to a distance-7 rotated surface code with 97 physical qubits under realistic superconducting-device noise including relaxation, dephasing, coherent miscalibration ($\delta_g = 0.1\%$), residual $ZZ$ crosstalk, and drive detuning, QMCtwin predicts syndrome-extraction biases and syndrome-to-string-parity correlations absent or suppressed in stochastic Pauli-twirled Clifford models.
motivation: Standard QEC decoders rely on syndrome statistics derived from stochastic Pauli or detector-error models, but Pauli twirling discards coherent phase information, nonunital drift, continuous-time effects of always-on couplings, and correlations from simultaneous Hamiltonian and dissipative evolution—all of which can affect decoder performance at scale.
method: QMCtwin uses real-time sign-problem-suppressed QMC to evolve the toggling-frame open-system master equation, stochastically compressing density matrices while preserving phase-sensitive and correlated dynamics. For a 97-qubit distance-7 syndrome-extraction round ($T_1 = 150$–$300$ µs, $T_\phi = 90$–$165$ µs, $J_{ij}/2\pi = 10$–$100$ kHz), observables are estimated directly from the QMC-generated stochastic density-matrix estimator.
result: QMCtwin reveals $O(10^{-2})$ syndrome-extraction biases and asymmetric ancilla-stabilizer disagreement probabilities (Z-type checks show $1.24 \times 10^{-2}$ vs. $1.65 \times 10^{-3}$ in Pauli baseline, a factor of 7.5 difference), alongside syndrome-to-string-parity mutual information nearly four times larger than the Pauli-twirled model ($\sim 0.11$–$0.14$ bits vs. $0.03$–$0.04$ bits).
